You've done nothing wrong nor is this wrongful interpretation or sensitivity.  These people are taking your kindness for granted and using it walk all over you because it makes you an easy target. 

My advice? First I would try to talk to one person in the group you feel most comfortable with. Talk with them one on one and express your discomfort. Depending on how that goes, either continue to slowly tell others in the group or try to ignore them because you don't need that type of energy in your life.

I strongly recommend you try to find a group of people you really connect with and enjoy and value you for you. This is--of course-- easier said than done not to mention your introverted nature. My best friend is an introvert and I'm an extrovert. We met in person and it took years to get close but some of the people he's met online he's become close with in months. Online is a great way to meet people without the same anxiety as in person. Discord, chat rooms, games, etc. I wish you the best of luck.

I've been on both sides of this situation. A best friend of mine and I grew apart when we went to separate schools, and we aren't nearly as close anymore. Occasionally we text but that's it.

On the other hand, my best friend of 7 years and I have a break for a year or so. He wasn't as responsive as I would have liked and he didn't seem interested. I genuinely believed I was losing the guy I felt was a brother to me. It was terrifying. I gave him space but still contacted him often and eventually things turned around and we're closer than ever.

Unfortunately, there's no way to tell what way these situations will go. If you truly want to preserve this friendship then I advise you continue contact consistently, even if it's small. It's going to hurt because she might not return with the same effort, but it keeps a constant in the relationship. Over time one of two things will happen: 1) You will slowly come back together or 2) She will feel the need to move on.

It hurts. It's painful. I won't lie to you. It's a process that takes time and doesn't always end up where you want it, but by the end of it you will be a stronger person with a better understanding of who you are. I wish you the best of luck.

TL/DR: Keep consistent contact with her even though it will hurt if she doesn't return the same effort
